description: HydroSource is a National Energy-Water digital platform run by Oak Ridge National Laboratory to help the hydropower community make data-driven decisions, with data, tools and publications for water power research. Its dataset listing can be filtered by publication year from 2010 to 2026 and by theme, and the themes include energy with 125 datasets, economics 63, environment 54 and resource assessment 30. Featured resources include the Existing Hydropower Assets Plant Database, 2025, a point-level dataset of hydropower plant locations and characteristics, the National Hydropower Fish Passage Database, and a dataset on technical potential for hydropower capacity at non-powered dams. There are also maps such as the Interactive National Hydropower Map and a story map, and tools such as the HydroSource Data Explorer, an environmental decision support toolkit for licensing and a fish passage webmap. Coverage is mainly the United States. Access: free and open in a web browser; each dataset page gives its own terms and no licence is stated on the home page, and the site warned of scheduled maintenance outages. Caveats: the platform is a collection, so quality and formats vary by dataset. It suits capacity planning and climate adaptation studies of hydropower, and relates to the ORNL environmental flow requirements record catalogued here.
